candidates.tagline: A $499 toothbrush with a built-in water jet — defeated by water
candidates.story: Dyson launched the CameraJet in September 2026 — a $499 electric toothbrush with a miniature camera, AI brushing guidance, and a built-in water jet — then pulled it from US, UK, and French stores within two weeks after buyers reported water seeping into the battery compartment and causing charging failures and dead units.
candidates.why_funny: The product's headline feature is a water jet; the thing that killed it was water — a toothbrush that couldn't survive its own bathroom.
candidates.alt: Dyson CameraJet AI electric toothbrush with camera lens visible in the handle, shown in product photography

candidates.tagline: Four years of precision hood engineering — aimed at the fuse box
candidates.story: Ford's Super Duty trucks ship with a hood cowling that funnels rainwater through a hole directly above the fuse box; when the lid fails to seal (common), water destroys the electronics for a ~$700 repair — and the 2027 fix is a small plastic diverter that also retrofits 2023–2026 trucks as a $20 drop-in part.
candidates.why_funny: Four model years to add a plastic rain deflector to stop the hood from acting as a precision irrigation system aimed at the most sensitive electronics in a $90,000 truck.
candidates.alt: 2027 Ford Super Duty pickup truck showing the front hood and grille where the water-drain design flaw was located
